assessment.nobel_worthiness: A powerful account of how technology, trade exposure, and task reallocation reshape labour demand and wage inequality, with large influence on empirical labour economics and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a highly coherent credited core for the task and trade-shock components of the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has had sustained influence and its central empirical patterns have been examined across settings over a substantial period.
uncertainties: The broad contribution combines several mechanisms, making a single bounded prize formulation difficult.
The relative scope of trade versus technology in the credited discovery requires careful framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility through population administrative data and made geographic variation in opportunity a central empirical economic question.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are an identifiable core for the listed administrative-data mobility contribution.
assessment.maturity: The measurement approach and resulting research program have diffused widely, while leaving ample time for scrutiny of interpretation and mechanisms.
uncertainties: Associations in mobility data do not by themselves establish the causal effects of places or policies.
The appropriate boundary between this contribution and related work on inequality, education, and neighbourhoods remains broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies supplied unusually direct evidence on labour-market discrimination and reshaped the empirical treatment of a question of first-order economic importance.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to the landmark correspondence-study evidence, with Charles a plausible co-credit for the broader listed program.
assessment.maturity: The design has become a durable tool, stimulated replication and refinement, and has consequences well beyond one labour-market setting.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify discrimination at particular margins and may not identify its aggregate contribution to inequality.
The wider literature has many important contributors, complicating comprehensive attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The long-run reconstruction of top incomes, wealth concentration, and offshore wealth substantially changed the empirical basis for studying inequality.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez, and Zucman are a coherent group for the linked data-building and measurement program specified here.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has generated a large and durable research literature and has made distributional measurement more central to economics.
uncertainties: Data construction, international comparability, and valuation choices remain consequential.
The contribution is strongest as measurement and documentation rather than as a settled unified causal theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme made imperfect competition on the employer side a central framework for understanding wages, labour-market power, and policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is especially closely associated with the modern monopsony framework; Naidu and Ashenfelter represent important theoretical and empirical strands in the listed contribution.
assessment.maturity: The idea has moved from a peripheral model to a major research agenda with substantial empirical application.
uncertainties: Empirical estimates of labour-market power are sensitive to market definition, institutional setting, and measurement.
The listed group spans distinct intellectual contributions that may not fit a single precise citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established early-life health and conditions as economically consequential determinants of later outcomes and advanced a dynamic view of human-capital formation.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha provide complementary and recognizable empirical and conceptual contributions to the stated discovery.
assessment.maturity: Its core insight has been tested across cohorts, shocks, and policy settings and now informs a wide interdisciplinary literature.
uncertainties: Long-run causal estimates often rely on setting-specific quasi-experimental variation.
The relationship between reduced-form early-life evidence and structural skill-formation mechanisms is not fully unified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods provided widely used tools for estimating economic relationships with persistent outcomes, fixed effects, and endogenous regressors.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Bond, and Blundell are the natural credited group for the principal estimator and its major extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are deeply embedded in applied econometrics and have received extensive theoretical and practical evaluation.
uncertainties: Finite-sample behavior, weak instruments, and instrument proliferation can materially affect applied results.
Its exceptional technical importance may be harder to present as a singular discovery with broad economic content.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work placed teacher quality, educational production, and accountability at the centre of economic analysis of schools and human capital.
assessment.attribution: Kane, Hanushek, and Woessmann are prominent and complementary contributors to the empirical and policy-facing strands of the listed agenda.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has been influential for decades and has produced extensive data, methodological development, and policy evaluation.
uncertainties: Evidence on accountability and teacher interventions varies markedly across institutional contexts.
The broad educational-production label encompasses several contributions with contested attribution and policy implications.
